item.title: Doubling the Angle on the bow
item.description:
The problem of doubling the angle on the bow with set due to current to find the distance from the light house at the time of second observation.

Step 1

A vessel while moving on a course steered represented by line AˉB\bar AB AˉB observes the bearing of a light house at D. After a certain duration, the vessel again observes the same light house at a bearing which is double the relative bearing at position A. The BˉC \bar BC BˉC represents the vessel’s drift during the duration of steaming between the two observations. The construction is done accordingly.

Step 2

From C line parallel to AB is drawn until it cuts line AD at F.CE is drawn parallel to AD until it cuts the line AB at E. AC is joined.

FC=CD=AE=(AB−BE) FC = CD = AE = (AB -BE) FC=CD=AE=(AB−BE)

and

∠EAD=∠CFD =∠CEB \angle EAD = \angle CFD\ = \angle CEB ∠EAD=∠CFD =∠CEB

because FC parallel to AB, because AD parallel to EC. Let Φ\PhiΦ = the relative angle between drift direction and course steered

Step 3

In △BCE \triangle BCE △BCE, Applying Sine formula,

sin(∠(BCE))BE=sin(∠(CBE))EC=sin(∠BEC)BC \frac{sin(\angle(BCE))}{BE} = \frac {sin(\angle (CBE))}{EC} = \frac {sin (\angle BEC)}{BC}BEsin(∠(BCE))​=ECsin(∠(CBE))​=BCsin(∠BEC)​

. We know ∠DAB=∠BEC=θ\angle DAB = \angle BEC = \theta ∠DAB=∠BEC=θ as DA is parallel to CE. We also the the distance of BC = drift of the ship during the interval between the two observations = d (assumed). Then from above equation.

sin(θ)d=sin∠BCEBE \frac {sin (\theta)}{d}= \frac {sin \angle BCE}{BE} dsin(θ)​=BEsin∠BCE​

Now

∠BCE=180°−θ−(180°−Φ) \angle BCE = 180\degree - \theta -( 180 \degree - \Phi )∠BCE=180°−θ−(180°−Φ)

because line EB extended is 180°180 \degree180° and in △BCE \triangle BCE △BCEsum of all angles180°180 \degree180°

∴∠BCE=Φ−θ \therefore \angle BCE = \Phi -\theta ∴∠BCE=Φ−θ

∴sin(θ)d=sin(Φ−θ)BE \therefore \frac { sin (\theta)}{d}= \frac{sin(\Phi - \theta) }{BE}∴dsin(θ)​=BEsin(Φ−θ)​

∴BE=d×sin(Φ−θ)sin(θ) \therefore BE = \frac { d \times sin(\Phi - \theta)}{sin (\theta)}∴BE=sin(θ)d×sin(Φ−θ)​

∴AE=AB(known)−BE(determined) \therefore AE = AB(known) - BE (determined) ∴AE=AB(known)−BE(determined)

AE = CD = distance off the light house at the time of second observation. This was the required solution.

item.title: Vertical sextant Angle
item.description:
Problems regarding Vertical Sextant Angle

Most Probably the given Data includes

  1. Height of eye.
  2. Distance of the mountain from the ship.
  3. Vertical Sextant Angle of the mountain Top.
  4. We will need to find out the height of the mountain.
